title: worktree-lock
description: The .worktree-lock document written in each slot worktree - the worktree's state of record, in sections: `claim` (the lock: who dispatched what, plus any shared resources held), `worker` (the conversation bound to this slot), and `turn` (an in-flight session turn). The filename is grandfathered legacy naming. Versioned via `v`; a document written by an older sm is upgraded by the elevator ladder in locks.mjs (elevateLock) before use. Sections are nullable; an all-null document is equivalent to no document.

cwd.description: absolute path of the slot worktree - the document's identity and source of truth; the slot label is derived from its basename

claim.description: the slot claim (the lock). null = unclaimed. Cleared by reset/prune; written by dispatch.

session.description: multiplexer session that claimed the slot

task.description: one-line task the slot was dispatched

issue.description: tracker issue id (e.g. sc-10132); this claim is its source of truth

transcript.description: DEPRECATED - legacy transcript path still parsed for pane-worker staleness and cross-wiring; no new writers

resources.description: shared machine-level resources this slot currently holds (browser, port, ...); each element is described by resource-lock.schema.json

worker.description: the conversation bound to this slot. null = no worker has ever run here. Survives reset; cleared by reset --hard-worker and slot rm.

agent.description: resolved agent instance name at last (re)spawn

model.description: model override in effect, if any

sessionId.description: CURRENT session id - written only from authoritative sources (a headless turn's result JSON), never inferred

createdAt.description: when this worker (conversation) began, epoch ms

turn.description: an in-flight session turn. null = no turn running. Holder identity is pid + start time (pid reuse cannot fake a live holder); stale turns are cleared lazily by the next serialized claimant.
